title: Штамп в паспорте  (The Stamp in the Passport)

segments.t: At the bar, Nagiyev proudly shows Vika and Kostya page fourteen of his passport: he is officially divorced from Kristina and did not lose his restaurant in the settlement.
Так, пойду организую шампанское для гостей.
Мне очень нравится, как ты работаешь.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'I got divorced!' Nagiyev proceeds calmly right here and lands on "razvyolsya" ("got divorced", built on "razvestis") to keep the statement grounded.
'Kristina Semyonovna, goodbye!' Nagiyev naturally shares this polite farewell at this moment using "do svidaniya" ("goodbye") — literally "until the next meeting", the standard Russian farewell.
'Page fourteen!' Nagiyev opens up warmly across the room, grounding the moment in plain reality.
'In the woods among the bears.' Focusing on the bears on the spot, Nagiyev chooses "medvedey" ("bears", from the root "medved") so Vika hears the exact meaning.
Так, пойду организую шампанское для гостей.
'Right, I will go arrange champagne for the guests.' Bringing up the champagne around Nagiyev, Vika chooses "shampanskoye" ("champagne") so Nagiyev gets the point right away.
'Go on, run, little rabbit.' Nagiyev cuts in lightly around Vika, grounding the moment in plain reality.
'Dmitry Vladimirovich, I congratulate you.' Kostya reacts promptly before Nagiyev and puts the weight on "pozdravlyayu" ("congratulations", from "pozdravlyat") as the exchange unfolds.
'Yes, my boy.' Pointing to the son on the spot, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
Мне очень нравится, как ты работаешь.
'I really like how you work.' Nagiyev replies quietly during the talk, so Kostya knows he is not just making small talk.
'Well done, champ.' Highlighting the handsome guy with Kostya, Nagiyev lands on "krasavchik" ("handsome guy") as the key everyday word here.

'Thank you.' Kostya readily directs this word of thanks in the exchange using "spasibo" ("thank you") — the everyday word for "thank you", which grew out of the old blessing "spasi Bog" ("God save you").
'I want to thank you.' Nagiyev follows up frankly hearing Kostya, to clear the air between them once and for all.
Так, пойду организую шампанское для гостей.
Мне очень нравится, как ты работаешь.
That brings Scene Four to a close. Listen for Nagiyev celebrating his freedom and looking for a way to reward Kostya at the bar. See you next time!
